Structural zeros

Source: R/ancombc_posthoc.r
structural_zeros.Rd

Finds the features that are absent, or nearly absent, from a group of samples (Kaul et al. 2017), as scikit-bio's struc_zero() and ANCOMBC's struc_zero option. A feature that is a structural zero in a group is differentially (less) abundant there, whatever a test of its abundance says, and should be left out of analyses of that group; one that is a structural zero in every group should be removed.

Usage

structural_zeros(counts, groups, data = NULL, margin = 1L, neg_lb = FALSE)

Arguments

counts

A numeric matrix of abundances (samples \(\times\) features), or any of the objects listed under Input Types: the table before any pseudocount or zero replacement.

groups

Each sample's group: a vector or factor with one value per sample, matched to the samples in counts by name when both are named, else in the same order. Or, when data is given, the name of one of its columns (or a vector with one value per row of data). Every distinct value is a group, numbers included; there must be at least two. A factor's unused levels are dropped.

data

Sample metadata: a data frame with one row per sample, holding the columns named in groups or strata. Rows are matched to the samples in counts by row name, and rows for other samples are ignored; without row names, they must be in the same order as the samples. Default: NULL.

margin

The margin containing samples. 1 if samples are rows, 2 if samples are columns. Ignored when counts is a special object class (e.g. phyloseq). Default: 1

neg_lb

FALSE (the default): a feature is a structural zero in a group when it is zero in every sample of that group. TRUE: when the lower bound of the 95% interval of its proportion of non-zero samples, \(\hat p - 1.96 \sqrt{\hat p (1 - \hat p) / n}\), is at most 0; recommended for large groups.

Value

A logical matrix, features \(\times\) groups, TRUE where the feature is a structural zero in the group. Groups are in sorted order (sort(method = 'radix'), as scikit-bio's), or in a factor's level order.

Input Types

The counts parameter is designed to accept a simple numeric matrix, but seamlessly supports objects from the following biological data packages:

  • phyloseq

  • rbiom

  • SummarizedExperiment

  • TreeSummarizedExperiment

For large datasets, standard matrix operations may be slow. See vignette('performance') for details on using optimized formats (e.g. sparse matrices) and parallel processing.

References

Kaul, A., Mandal, S., Davidov, O., & Peddada, S. D. (2017). Analysis of microbiome data in the presence of excess zeros. Frontiers in Microbiology, 8, 2114.

See also

ancombc(), ancombc_global().

Examples

    x <- rbind(
      c( 7, 1,  0, 11,  3,  1), c( 1, 1, 0, 13, 13,  0),
      c(11, 5,  0,  1,  4,  1), c( 2, 2, 0, 16,  4,  0),
      c( 0, 1,  0,  0,  6,  0), c(14, 8, 7,  9,  0,  5),
      c( 0, 7,  4,  1,  0, 26), c( 8, 1, 4, 28,  0, 10),
      c( 2, 2,  2,  4,  0,  5), c( 6, 4, 10,  1,  0,  9) )
    colnames(x) <- paste0('f', 0:5)
    grp <- rep(c('treatment', 'placebo'), each = 5)
    structural_zeros(x, grp)
#>    placebo treatment
#> f0   FALSE     FALSE
#> f1   FALSE     FALSE
#> f2   FALSE      TRUE
#> f3   FALSE     FALSE
#> f4    TRUE     FALSE
#> f5   FALSE     FALSE
    structural_zeros(x, grp, neg_lb = TRUE)
#>    placebo treatment
#> f0   FALSE     FALSE
#> f1   FALSE     FALSE
#> f2   FALSE      TRUE
#> f3   FALSE     FALSE
#> f4    TRUE     FALSE
#> f5   FALSE      TRUE
